extra.message: Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) in Jinja2 Template via 'fragment' parameter — Remote code execution on the server, arbitrary file read, and complete application compromise through Jinja2 template engine exploitation. [verified: User-controlled GET 'fragment' interpolated directly into Jinja2 Template('Result: '+fragment).render() at line 133 with no sandboxing; _wrk_gate present but no input neutralization.]

Server-Side Template Injection (SSTI) via Jinja2 Template with user-controlled fragment — Remote code execution on the server through Jinja2 template engine [verified: Duplicate of finding [1]/[13]: same SSTI via Jinja2 Template() with user-controlled 'fragment'.]

OS Command Injection via user-controlled 'host' parameter in ping command — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process, enabling full system compromise, data exfiltration, and lateral movement. [verified: User-controlled GET 'host' concatenated unsanitized into os.system('ping -c 1 '+host) at line 174; _wrk_gate token check exists but does not sanitize shell metacharacters.]

Command injection via user-controlled host parameter in ping command — Remote code execution on the server with the privileges of the Django process [verified: Duplicate of finding [0]/[14]: same command injection via os.system with user-controlled 'host'.]

DEBUG=True by default with hardcoded SECRET_KEY — Full information disclosure (database queries, file paths, settings, local variables in tracebacks) to unauthenticated users, plus session forgery and privilege escalation via the known SECRET_KEY. [verified: Combines DEBUG=True default (error-page info disclosure + unauthenticated media serving) with a hardcoded, publicly-visible SECRET_KEY default (session/token forgery); no production settings module or conditional override exists for either.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY allowing session forgery and token manipulation — Complete compromise of session integrity — attackers can forge authenticated sessions for any user, including school admins, and craft valid password-reset tokens to take over accounts. [verified: SECRET_KEY falls back to the hardcoded literal 'local-dev-insecure-change-me' committed in version control; if DJANGO_SECRET_KEY env var is absent, an attacker who knows this key can forge session cookies, CSRF tokens, and password-reset tokens for any user.]

Hardcoded default Django SECRET_KEY allows session and token forgery — Session hijacking, CSRF bypass, password reset token forgery leading to account takeover [verified: Same hardcoded SECRET_KEY default as finding 1 — the literal 'local-dev-insecure-change-me' in settings.py line 19 is the runtime fallback when DJANGO_SECRET_KEY is not provided, enabling session forgery and account takeover.]

Path Traversal leading to Arbitrary File Write via user-controlled 'name' parameter — Arbitrary file write anywhere the Django process has write access, enabling code execution through overwriting Python files, cron jobs, or other executable paths. [verified: GET 'name' used directly as Path component at line 140 (BASE_EXPORT_DIR/name) with mkdir creating intermediate dirs; no path normalization or sanitization against traversal.]

XML External Entity (XXE) injection via permissive lxml XMLParser on untrusted request body — Arbitrary local file disclosure, server-side request forgery, and denial of service through XML entity expansion attacks. [verified: lxml XMLParser(load_dtd=True,resolve_entities=True,no_network=False) parses raw request.body at line 159 enabling external entity resolution; _wrk_gate present but no XML sanitization.]

DEBUG=True enabled by default exposing error details and unprotected media files — Information disclosure of source code, database schemas, settings (including partially redacted secrets), and unrestricted access to uploaded media files including student submissions and course documents. [verified: DEBUG defaults to True via env_bool('DJANGO_DEBUG', True) with no production override file or force-false guard; urls.py serves all uploaded media files without authentication when DEBUG=True, exposing student submissions and course documents to anyone who guesses a file path.]

Django DEBUG mode enabled by default leaks sensitive information in error pages — Exposure of environment variables, database configuration, secret keys, and application internals through verbose error pages [verified: Same DEBUG=True default as finding 0 — env_bool('DJANGO_DEBUG', True) keeps debug mode on without any environment guard; exposes detailed error tracebacks with settings, SQL, and local variables, plus serves media files without auth.]

Missing Secure flag on session and CSRF cookies — Session hijacking via network sniffing - an attacker on the same network (public Wi-Fi, compromised router) can capture session cookies and impersonate any user including school admins. [verified: SESSION_COOKIE_SECURE is never set and defaults to False; no SECURE_SSL_REDIRECT or other HTTPS enforcement exists, so session cookies can be transmitted over unencrypted HTTP where network attackers can intercept them.]

Missing Rate Limiting on Authentication Endpoints — Brute-force attacks on user passwords, credential stuffing, and DoS via repeated authentication requests - no mechanism prevents an attacker from making unlimited login or password-reset attempts. [verified: No rate-limiting package (django-ratelimit, django-axes) installed, no throttling middleware in MIDDLEWARE, and no custom decorators exist on login (/accounts/login/), password-reset, invitation acceptance, or ops endpoints — brute-force is unrestricted.]

Media files publicly accessible without authentication when DEBUG=True — Unauthenticated access to private student submission attachments, course resources, and other uploaded files via direct URL [verified: DEBUG defaults to True and triggers static() serving of MEDIA_URL /media/ without authentication, bypassing the can_download_document permission checks enforced on /documents/<pk>/download/; unauthenticated users can directly fetch submission attachments, course resources, and export files.]

Plaintext passwords retained on disk in import CSV files after processing — An attacker with filesystem access or who can enumerate media URLs can recover plaintext user passwords from persisted CSV import files, enabling credential theft and account takeover across the LMS user base. [verified: CSV files with a plaintext 'password' column are saved to disk via save_document() at predictable MEDIA_ROOT paths and never deleted after process_import_job() hashes the passwords; ImportJob.document uses on_delete=SET_NULL so no cascade cleanup occurs, and DEBUG=True (the default) serves media/ statically without auth, leaving plaintext credentials persistently reachable.]

Missing Rate Limiting on authentication endpoints enabling brute-force attacks — Unlimited brute-force password guessing on login, email spam via repeated password-reset requests, and invitation token enumeration without any throttling or lockout protection. [verified: No rate-limiting middleware (django-axes, throttling) is installed in MIDDLEWARE or anywhere in the codebase; LoginView at /accounts/login/ is configured without the rate_limit parameter (Django 5.2 supports it but it is unused), PasswordResetView lacks email-send throttling, accept_invitation loops over token-guessing with no backoff, and API endpoints have no request throttling — brute-force is ]

Reflected Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) — Arbitrary JavaScript execution in the victim's browser - can steal cookies, perform actions as the victim, and exfiltrate sensitive data from the LMS. [verified: Duplicate of finding [4]: same reflected XSS via unescaped 'copyline' in HTML response at line 30.]

Open Redirect via user-controlled 'lane' parameter — Phishing and social engineering attacks by redirecting authenticated users to attacker-controlled websites that may mimic the LMS login page. [verified: GET/POST 'lane' passed directly to Django redirect() at line 66 with no URL validation or allowlist; _wrk_gate present but no destination filtering.]

Path Traversal with Sensitive PII Storage via user-controlled 'ref' parameter — Arbitrary JSON file write to attacker-chosen filesystem paths, plus plaintext storage of synthetic PII (SSN, credit card numbers) on disk. [verified: GET 'ref' interpolated into BASE_EXPORT_DIR/f'{ref}.json' at line 80 with no traversal sanitization; limited to .json extension but allows writing attacker-controlled PII to arbitrary locations.]

Sensitive PII (SSN, credit card numbers) stored in plaintext on filesystem — Exposure of sensitive personal identifiable information if the filesystem is compromised [verified: Duplicate of finding [25]: same plaintext PII storage (SSN/card in JSON on disk).]

Sensitive PII Stored in Plaintext on Filesystem — Plaintext storage of Social Security Numbers and credit card numbers on disk - accessible via path traversal, backup exposure, or filesystem compromise. [verified: SSN and credit card values from GET params written as plain JSON to disk at line 83 via course_vault_stash_245; _wrk_gate present but data stored unencrypted with no access controls.]

Missing Authentication on Ops Endpoint (course_identity_ping_341) — Unauthenticated access to an internal operations endpoint, bypassing the shared-token gate that protects all other /ops/ routes. [verified: course_identity_ping_341 at line 93 is the only /ops/ endpoint lacking the _wrk_gate(request) token check, reachable at /ops/identity/course-ping-341/ per urls.py:52 with no middleware or decorator compensating; the shared-token gate required by the threat model is genuinely absent on this path.]

CORS Misconfiguration — arbitrary origin allowed with credentials — Cross-origin requests with credentials (cookies) allowed from any origin, enabling CSRF-like attacks against ops endpoints from arbitrary malicious websites. [verified: Origin header echoed as Access-Control-Allow-Origin with credentials:true at lines 117-118; any origin can make credentialed cross-origin requests once past _wrk_gate.]

Unbounded file write consumes disk space enabling denial of service — Disk exhaustion leading to denial of service for all application functions [verified: request.body written to disk via target.write_bytes() at line 143 with no size limit; _wrk_gate present but token-holder can exhaust disk via large payloads.]

Sensitive Data in Logs — Authorization header and request body written to application logs — Exposure of authentication tokens, API keys, and sensitive request data in application logs, leading to credential theft and unauthorized access. [verified: Authorization header logged via logger.warning at line 72 alongside full request body; _wrk_gate restricts access but legitimate internal calls could leak tokens to logs.]

Sensitive Data (Bearer Tokens) Written to Logs — Credential leakage - API keys, session tokens, and other secrets in the Authorization header are persisted in log files where they can be accessed by anyone with log read access, or leaked through log aggregation systems. [verified: Duplicate of finding [7]: same Authorization header logging via logger.warning at line 72.]
